Theme

Latin word

petō

petō, petere, petīvī (petiī), petītum

verb, third conjugation, with an accusative

apply for, seek (a post); stand for (office); go for, fetch (a thing); make for, travel to (a place); seek, aim at; ask for, request

In this lexicon

  • apply

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 1.1.2: nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt; Liv. 26.18.7: professus sē petere; Traupman 180

  • get

    the recommended word · classical · Gell. 17.8.8: nōnne īs curriculō atque oleum petis?; Plin. NH 9.169: petere Brundisium ostreās (Lewis & Short); Traupman 314

  • head for

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.125: gruēs loca calidiōra petentēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 204; Traupman 326

  • pursue

    also used · classical · Sall. C. 54.5: glōriam (Lewis & Short); Cic. Or. 56: ēloquentiae prīncipātum (Lewis & Short)

  • request

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 1.9.2: petō abs tē ut haec dīligenter cūrēs; Cic. Fam. 9.13.3: petō igitur ā tē vel, sī pateris, ōrō ut …

Examples

  • nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt quī, sī in nostrum annum reciderit, firmior candidātus fore videātur

    For of those now standing there is no one who, if his election falls in my year, would look like a stronger candidate.Cic. Att. 1.1.2

    In the entry for apply

  • quattuor et vīgintī fermē annōs nātus, professus sē petere, in superiōre unde cōnspicī posset locō cōnstitit

    About twenty-four years old, he declared that he was standing, and took his place on higher ground where everyone could see him.Liv. 26.18.7
